standards.name: WCAG 2.2 — Contrast (Minimum)
standards.rule: Normal text requires at least 4.5:1 contrast; large text requires at least 3:1.

standards.name: WCAG 2.2 — Use of Color
standards.rule: Color cannot be the only visual means of communicating meaning, state or required action.

standards.name: WCAG 2.2 — Non-text Contrast
standards.rule: Essential component boundaries, states and graphical objects require at least 3:1 contrast where the criterion applies.

standards.name: CSS Color Module Level 4
standards.rule: Use modern perceptual color spaces such as OKLCH deliberately, with tested gamut fallbacks where project support requires them.

standards.name: Material Design 3 — Color roles
standards.rule: Map palette primitives to semantic roles such as surface, on-surface, primary and on-primary instead of styling components with raw values.

standards.name: Radix Colors — Understanding the scale
standards.rule: Assign predictable scale steps to backgrounds, interactive states, borders, solid fills and text.

standards.name: MDN — color-scheme
standards.rule: Declare supported schemes and design light and dark themes as separate tested mappings, including native controls.

packages.name: Radix Colors
strengths: documented background, border and text usage
caveats: target contrast still depends on the exact foreground/background pair
brand mapping and visual review remain project-specific

packages.name: Adobe Leonardo Contrast Colors
strengths: contrast is an input to generation
caveats: generated output requires semantic role mapping
verify selected contrast method and final rendered context

packages.name: Material Color Utilities
caveats: Material defaults are not a substitute for brand art direction
deprecated Scheme APIs must not be used for new work

packages.name: Primer Primitives
caveats: do not copy GitHub brand expression
adopt the token architecture or package only when it fits the product

packages.name: Open Props
caveats: import only the modules actually used
raw props must be remapped to semantic project tokens

packages.name: Culori
caveats: it computes colors but does not choose semantic roles
contrast and gamut must be verified after transformations

packages.name: Color.js
strengths: maintained by CSS Color specification editors
caveats: select one documented contrast policy per project
wide-gamut output needs an intentional fallback strategy
